Community layers

See how occasional, returning, regular, and core participants shape conversation.

Audience

Layer definitions

Drop-in: one stream. Returning: two or three streams. Regular: four to seven streams. Core: eight or more streams. Bar length is the number of chatters; the annotation shows the share of conversation produced.

Engagement landscape

Cross stream breadth with message intensity to reveal distinct participation patterns.

Matrix

Chatter flows

Follow individual chatters through streams and into title topics or tags.

Relationship view

About this view

Each path follows an observed chatter into a stream and then into the topic or normalized title tag attached to that stream. Use the Streams and Chatters selectors to search the complete catalogs; filtering options never silently changes the chart. Path width uses the selected engagement measure. When a stream has several normalized tags, its outgoing flow is divided evenly so engagement is not duplicated. View contribution uses the latest canonical video performance and is not recalculated when streams are filtered.

Chatter–stream participation

Compare attendance patterns and identify chatters who move through similar streams.

Heatmap

About this view

Rows place people with similar stream-attendance patterns near one another. A shared vertical pattern means two chatters participated in many of the same selected streams. Switch the cell measure between attendance and messages, or restore a simple highest-activity row order.

Stream audience overlap

Compare shared chatter audiences across streams with Jaccard similarity.

Network matrix

About this view

Darker purple indicates that two streams share a larger proportion of their combined chatter audience. Hover for the shared-chatter count and exact similarity. Use Compare to choose any videos in the current scope; the matrix recalculates immediately for that subset. The diagonal is gray because each stream is being compared with itself.
